historical_reviews.v3_1: A live removal is safe only after proving the selected controller, every namespace and all dependent mounts/swap/RAID/LVM consumers are inactive. Acceptance then requires an ordered disappearance event with no errors, followed by reappearance of the same serial at the expected bay/BDF and restoration of negotiated link and BMC state; a final `nvme list` alone loses the transition.

original_test_intent: Validate supported under-OS hot-remove and hot-add recovery for each E1.S NVMe SSD across OS enumeration, BMC/IPMI visibility and PCIe link state.
original_method: Map every target serial/controller/namespace/BDF/bay, prove it is hot-swap capable and fully quiesced, collect baseline state, have an authorized operator live-remove one device while the Agent records ordered OS/BMC/PCIe disappearance, reinsert the same device and record clean enumeration/link/health recovery, then gate the next drive on complete stabilization.
manual_activity: A storage/platform owner approves every hot-swap bay and drive state; an authorized operator performs each physical removal/reinsertion while the Agent observes read-only surfaces.
required_inputs: Proof of no mounts, swap, RAID, LVM, device-mapper or active I/O dependencies
safety_requirements: Never remove a mounted, active or dependency-bearing device
Confirm physical bay and serial before contact
Handle one drive at a time
Use only vendor-approved hot-swap bays and sequence
Do not substitute PCIe reset or blind rescan
Stop immediately on I/O, filesystem, AER, link, temperature or BMC error
Do not continue after incomplete recovery
Do not retry a failed cycle
Do not alter namespaces or format media
agent_execution_scope: Confirm expected disappearance without residual consumers or errors
Capture same-device insertion and full link/health recovery
Compare each transition to the approved matrix
Archive evidence and report without verdict
engineer_actions: Approve bay capability, order and safe drive state
Stop and lead recovery after any abnormal event
Confirm whether degraded link or BMC lag is acceptable
Decide PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED per drive

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Enumeration and `dmesg -T` are necessary but do not prove safe pre-removal dependency state, BMC Web/IPMI behavior, BDF speed/bandwidth or same-serial recovery, and the wording understates the live-removal half of this case.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Continuously collect complete read-only `lsblk`/mount dependency, NVMe controller, kernel, BMC/IPMI and per-BDF link evidence while the operator performs one approved live remove/reinsert cycle; never automate physical action or force discovery.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Every approved E1.S SSD, both hot-remove and hot-add transitions, all specified observation surfaces and the 30-minute estimate remain in scope.

modernized_recommendation.status: SERIALIZED LIVE E1S REMOVE-ADD STATE-MACHINE VALIDATION
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: For each safe drive, prove no consumers, timestamp physical removal and OS/BMC/PCIe disappearance, then bind reinsertion to the same serial and require namespace, link, health and management recovery before proceeding.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Defines `normal` as a measurable ordered transition, adds dependency closure and exact same-device recovery while preserving the original physical sequence.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A final healthy inventory can conceal removal errors, stale namespaces, AER events, BMC mismatches or reinsertion of the wrong drive; continuous event evidence is required.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Live removal can corrupt data or destabilize the PCIe tree even when the bay is nominally hot-swappable; physical seating and ESD handling remain human responsibilities.

project_override_considerations: Approve which E1.S bays support both surprise removal and addition, required software quiesce steps, device-disappearance and recovery deadlines, expected BMC resources, acceptable AER policy and link-training tolerance.
expected_evidence: Approved hot-swap procedure and SUT/OS/kernel/backplane identity
Drive serial-controller-namespace-BDF-bay map plus full no-consumer proof
Per-drive complete baseline/removal/reinsertion nvme, lsblk, dependency, lspci, BMC/IPMI and kernel event timeline
Same-serial namespace/link/health recovery and no-error proof
Final full inventory, preserved logs, no-reset/no-format/no-retry audit and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items and Procedure consistently specify live per-drive hot-plug with OS, BMC and PCIe checks. The broad `normal` criterion is under-defined but does not contradict the stated operation.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The live remove/add purpose and required surfaces are identifiable. Vendor capability, safe device state and operator support are finite prerequisites, so classification is REQUIRES.

review_improvement: Turns vague normality into a per-drive transition contract that proves dependency safety, ordered removal, same-device return and complete OS/BMC/PCIe recovery.
independent_technical_reasoning: The kernel may remove a controller while users still hold namespace or mapper references, so absence from `nvme list` is not proof of safe removal. Conversely, reappearance of a namespace does not prove the same serial returned or that the PCIe link trained at the expected width. The correctness unit is the whole state transition anchored by serial and bay, with consumers closed before removal and every surface reconciled after insertion.
